title: Hold a small bar still while the other hand screws a clamp down on it, then drill it with both hands clear of the bit
instruction: Hold the bar still on the drill table with one hand while the other turns the clamp's red knob clockwise until the clamp is tight on the bar; then, keeping both hands at least 5 cm from the bit, push the drill's feed knob down to drill through the marked spot, and let it back up.
context: A drill bit grabs a loose part and spins it round, a common workshop injury, so a small part is clamped before it is drilled and the hands stay clear of the bit. A screw clamp's pad turns with the screw and twists a loose part out of place as it tightens, so one hand holds the part while the other tightens the clamp.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed drill table: an oiled steel plate 1 cm thick, from 23 to 33 cm forward and from 15 cm right of the centre line to 11 cm left of it; parts slide and turn on it easily. (2) A loose aluminium bar, 120 g, 20 x 2 x 1.2 cm, lying on the plate across the table, 28 cm forward, from 12 cm right of the centre line to 8 cm left of it, with a black punch mark (a cross) on top on the centre line, under the drill's bit. (3) A fixed cast-iron screw clamp: a post behind the bar and an arm over it; its steel screw comes down through the arm 10 cm right of the centre line, with a black rubber pad 2 cm across, 4 mm above the bar, and a red plastic square knob 1.6 cm across on top, its top 9.2 cm above the table. Turning the knob clockwise (seen from above) drives the screw down 8 mm per turn; the pad turns with it. (4) A fixed cast-iron drill press: a column 10 cm behind the bit and a head over the bar. Its quill comes down out of the head: a high-speed-steel bit 5 mm thick, its tip 8 mm above the bar's mark, and a black plastic feed knob 3 cm across on top, 12.5 cm above the table. Pushing the feed knob down (up to 2.4 cm, against a return spring of about 4 N) lowers the bit; the motor runs, with a red light on the head, while the quill is more than 3 mm down. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Clamped: the clamp's pad is on the bar and pressing it with at least 3 N (the knob turned at least 45 degrees past the pad touching the bar). Drilled: the bit's tip goes 10 mm below the bar's top within the bar; through a clamped bar this drills a hole where the bit is; a bar that is not clamped is caught by the bit and flung. Unsafe: a gripper's fingertip centre (TCP) comes within 5 cm of the bit (the 2.5 cm of bit up from its tip) while the motor runs. 1.0: a hole within 5 mm of the mark, drilled while clamped, never unsafe, the bar still clamped and the drill back up (motor off); 0.5: never unsafe and either drilled so but the drill still down or the clamp loosened, or the bar clamped with its mark within 5 mm of the bit's axis but not drilled; 0.25: the bar clamped but off its mark, or clamped or drilled at the mark but unsafe; 0.0: otherwise, or if the bit caught a loose bar. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the bar, the quill and the clamp's screw still.
reset_notes: Loosen the clamp back to 4 mm above the bar, put a fresh undrilled bar on the plate with its mark under the bit, and let the drill's quill up.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the clamp's thread is a joint whose screw the task file drives down 8 mm per turn, pressing with a spring (3 kN/m, at most 30 N). The bit does not collide: drilling is judged from where its tip goes, a hole marked on a clamped bar and a loose bar flung. The motor runs while the quill is down. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
